hot_topics.topic: Binance Crypto Exchange Suffers Record Hack, North Korea Suspected
hot_topics.synthesis: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, endured a record-breaking $6.3 billion hack, leading to the temporary suspension of all withdrawals. Investigations by blockchain intelligence firms and law enforcement quickly linked the sophisticated cyber-attack to North Korean hackers, who reportedly gained access through an employee's laptop and converted billions into untraceable assets. The rapid execution of the attack, completed in just 20 minutes, highlights the advanced capabilities of the perpetrators.

hot_topics.topic: GM Settles for $220 Million Over Driver Data Sales
hot_topics.synthesis: General Motors has reached a $220 million settlement with 35 states and the District of Columbia after allegedly selling customer driving data from its Smart Driver system to insurance brokers without explicit consent. The automaker had previously settled with the FTC, resulting in the discontinuation of the Smart Driver program and a five-year ban on sharing certain driver behavior and geolocation data. This collective legal action underscores growing regulatory and public concern over automotive data privacy practices.

hot_topics.topic: Reddit Shifts to Mandatory Log-in for All Users
hot_topics.synthesis: Reddit is transitioning to a 'logged-in-only experience' across its platform, a strategic move confirmed by CEO Steve Huffman in response to evolving online information consumption and the impact of AI on search traffic. This change aims to improve user engagement through better ad targeting, protect Reddit's extensive data corpus, and help the platform adapt to emerging global regulations. The company anticipates that requiring users to log in will also enhance new user retention and strengthen its business model.

hot_topics.topic: Tech Stocks Fall as AI Costs and Google's Ad Revenue Impact Fuel Market Fears
hot_topics.synthesis: US tech stocks have experienced sharp declines, with Intel shares falling and the Nasdaq reaching a two-month low, primarily driven by investor apprehension over the escalating costs of AI development, which are nearing $1 trillion. This market anxiety is further intensified by major companies like Google, which revealed that its own AI search summaries are negatively impacting traditional ad revenue. The confluence of massive AI investment requirements and disruptive impacts on core business models signals a significant financial challenge for the tech sector.

hot_topics.topic: DOJ Cracks Down on International AI-Assisted Student Loan Fraud
hot_topics.synthesis: The U.S. Department of Justice has initiated the first major federal crackdown on 'ghost students,' an international scheme that used stolen identities and, in part, artificial intelligence to defraud student loan programs of millions of dollars. Five individuals, including those linked to Kenyan nationals, have been charged, and over $750,000 in cryptocurrency seized. This action marks a significant expansion of law enforcement efforts to combat sophisticated fraud operations leveraging AI on a global scale.

hot_topics.topic: Waymo and Toyota Deepen Partnership for Global Robotaxi Deployment
hot_topics.synthesis: Waymo is strengthening its strategic alliance with Toyota, announcing plans to deploy purpose-built bZ4X electric vehicles for robotaxi services in Tokyo next year, with expansion also slated for the UK. This collaboration will see Waymo's self-driving technology integrated directly onto Toyota's assembly lines, rather than as a post-manufacturing modification. The partnership leverages the expertise of both companies, combining Toyota's manufacturing prowess with Waymo's leadership in autonomous driving to scale global robotaxi operations.

hot_topics.topic: Rivian Advances Autonomous Driving and AI Integration
hot_topics.synthesis: Rivian is aggressively pursuing its autonomous vehicle ambitions, with plans to introduce a point-to-point hands-free driving feature to employees in 2026 and to customers by 2027, followed by robotaxi launches in partnership with Uber in 2028. The company has also expanded its joint venture with Volkswagen to incorporate an AI assistant, though the financial impact on their $5.8 billion venture remains undisclosed. These initiatives signify Rivian's deep commitment to integrating advanced AI into its automotive and mobility offerings.

hot_topics.topic: Alaska Senate Race Embroiled in 'Spoiler Candidate' Allegations
hot_topics.synthesis: The Alaska Senate race has become mired in controversy after the incumbent Republican senator and his allies accused Democrats of recruiting a 'spoiler candidate' named Dan J. Sullivan to confuse voters. These claims allege an attempt to dilute support for the incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, prompting the state's governor to order an investigation. The dispute highlights concerns about political tactics and election integrity in a closely watched race.

hot_topics.topic: US Midterm Elections See Surge in Early Voting Amidst Voter Distrust and Political Challenges
hot_topics.synthesis: The upcoming US midterm elections are marked by a significant surge in early voting, particularly among Hispanic voters, indicating high engagement in key battleground counties. Despite this, a recent poll reveals widespread public distrust in political surveys, with only 25% of Americans believing they accurately estimate votes. Key political narratives include Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro's campaign with potential 2028 presidential implications, a shift in Cuban voter sentiment against Republican immigration policies, and the Democratic party grappling with an 'identity crisis.' These dynamics underscore a highly competitive and complex electoral landscape that holds significant implications for both parties and figures like former President Trump.

items.title: In praise of the dilettante
items.summary: The essay praises the dilettante as an "anti-hero" suited for a hyper-specialized age, characterized as a wayfaring cosmopolitan who avoids being stuck in narrow expertise. This perspective advocates for broad intellectual exploration over deep specialization.

items.title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there's no plug involved
items.summary: Nissan is launching the 2027 Rogue Hybrid with its e-Power series hybrid system, where the 1.5L engine acts solely as a generator for the electric motor, providing an EV-like driving experience without a plug. This system allows the engine to operate at a high thermal efficiency by optimizing it for battery charging rather than direct wheel drive.

items.title: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
items.summary: Fujifilm plans a $63 million investment to increase its magnetic tape production capacity fivefold by fiscal year 2028, driven by the exponential growth in data demand fueled by generative AI. This expansion will primarily focus on producing the latest-generation FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10 tape.

items.title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
items.summary: General Motors will pay $220 million to the District of Columbia and 35 states for selling customer driving data from its Smart Driver system to insurance brokers without explicit consent. GM previously settled with the FTC, discontinuing Smart Driver and agreeing to a five-year ban on sharing certain driver data.

items.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
items.summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has suspended all withdrawals following a hack estimated to have impacted about $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion frozen. Analysts believe the attackers converted $3.3 billion into unfrozen digital assets and are working to cash them out.

items.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
items.summary: A rare Martian meteorite, Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert, has been identified as forming at least 4.1 billion years ago, providing insights into the planet's ancient crust. This makes it one of only three genuinely ancient Martian meteorites known, with its rarity possibly due to the filtering effect of large impact events needed to launch rocks off Mars.

items.title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
items.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman announced that the platform will transition to a "logged-in-only experience" to improve user engagement, enable better ad targeting, and protect access to Reddit's valuable data corpus. This change is also intended to help Reddit retain new users and adapt to emerging regulations.

items.title: Thousands of “ghost students” use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
items.summary: The US Department of Justice has charged five individuals in the first major federal crackdown on "ghost students" who used stolen identities and partly AI to defraud student loan programs. The DOJ seized over $750,000 in cryptocurrency from a network linked to Kenyan nationals and warned that the crackdown is expanding globally.

items.title: Your Book Review: The History And Adventures Of An Atom
items.summary: A book review highlights Tobias Smollett’s 1769 novel, *The History and Adventures of an Atom*, as exceptionally weird and influential in the history of the novel. The review explores how 18th-century novels broke from previous forms and the unique narrative choices that define Smollett's work.

items.title: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete who soiled herself in race tells BBC
items.summary: Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk admitted to the BBC that her determination to win a race in September clouded her judgment, leading her to soil herself during the competition. She stated she made the wrong decision during the intense event.

items.title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
items.summary: A temporary ceasefire has brought a rare period of quiet to Kherson, offering residents a brief glimpse of normal life, but they remain fearful of what will happen once fighting resumes. This precarious peace highlights the ongoing uncertainty in the region.

items.title: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot
items.summary: An Alaska Senate candidate denies knowledge of an alleged plot to put two individuals named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, which the incumbent Republican senator and allies claim was an attempt to confuse voters. The state's governor has ordered an investigation into these claims.

items.title: Canada stops using 'avalanche dogs' for rescues in Rocky Mountains, stirring outrage
items.summary: Canada has ended its 55-year-old avalanche dog rescue program in the Rocky Mountains due to government budget cuts, sparking outrage. The decision impacts a program that has historically found missing hikers and children.

items.title: China denies allegations of spy operation targeting Nvidia CEO
items.summary: China has denied allegations of a spy operation targeting Nvidia's CEO, following reports that US intelligence officials believe a Chinese businesswoman was gathering information for Beijing on the chip-making giant. The denial comes amid escalating tensions over technology and espionage.

items.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.summary: Crypto giant Binance is trying to recover $6.3 billion stolen in a complex cyber-attack believed to be linked to North Korea, marking the largest hack of its kind. The company is actively working to mitigate the impact of this unprecedented security breach.

items.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
items.summary: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy attributed Egypt's press crackdown to the US decision to waive a human rights condition on military aid. He argues that this action paved the way for arrests of journalists.

items.title: Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix
items.summary: Regardless of midterm election results, the Democratic party faces an identity crisis and tough questions about its platform and representation. This signals a difficult path ahead for the party in defining its future.

items.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
items.summary: The G20 "family photo" was canceled after European foreign ministers refused to be pictured with Russian minister Sergei Lavrov at the Atlanta summit. This highlights ongoing diplomatic tensions and protest against Russia's presence.

items.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
items.summary: Google's market value plunged by $500 billion, hitting a six-month low, after the company revealed that its own AI search summaries were negatively impacting ad revenue. This indicates a significant financial consequence of AI integration for its core business model.

items.title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam
items.summary: Kenyans are among those charged in a $130 million US ghost student scam that allegedly used stolen identities to claim US student aid. The scheme involved an international network of fraudsters.

items.title: Human rights lawyer couple sentenced to 10 years' prison in Pakistan
items.summary: A human rights lawyer couple, Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, have been sentenced to 10 years in prison in Pakistan for an incident that occurred in 2024. Their charges relate to an event during England's cricket tour of Pakistan.

items.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
items.summary: Hundreds of people were evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during a rare Ukraine ceasefire, though many residents chose to remain despite the dangers. This temporary halt in fighting offered a brief respite for the front-line town.

items.title: Indians turn to start-ups to care for ageing parents as young become more mobile
items.summary: Changing family structures in India, driven by increased mobility among the young, are leading to a surge in demand for startups offering eldercare services. This trend reflects evolving societal needs and business opportunities in India.

items.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
items.summary: The Israeli opposition accuses Prime Minister Netanyahu of trying to "delegitimise" the election, after his Likud party alleged foreign interference and claimed Arab-led parties "stole" the election following his coalition's loss of majority. These accusations deepen political divisions in Israel.

items.title: Many Cubans voted for Trump - now they're turning on Republican immigration policies
items.summary: Many Cuban voters who previously supported Trump are now turning against Republican immigration policies, suggesting a potential shift in their voting patterns. This frustration could impact Republican performance at the ballot box.

items.title: More than 43 million ballots cast so far in midterms early voting surge
items.summary: Over 43 million ballots have been cast in the midterms' early voting, with Hispanic voters contributing significantly to numbers that outpace previous elections in some battleground counties. This surge suggests strong voter engagement ahead of Election Day.

items.title: Mushroom murderer fails to overturn convictions in Australian court challenge
items.summary: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson failed to overturn her convictions in an appeals court, with judges dismissing all seven grounds of her challenge. The prosecution's appeal for a longer non-parole period was also agreed upon.

items.title: New York police will now investigate Cornell sex complaints, governor says
items.summary: New York police will now investigate sex complaints at Cornell University, a change announced amid backlash over the school's handling of gang rape allegations involving a fraternity. This shift aims to improve the investigation process for such serious accusations.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
items.summary: Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV became the first pontiff to vote in a US election, mailing in a ballot for the midterm elections. His vote, amid a tense relationship with Trump, will help decide control of the US Congress.

items.title: Prominent Russian newspaper shuts down under pressure from authorities
items.summary: Novaya Gazeta, a prominent independent Russian news outlet, has shut down after three decades due to pressure from authorities. Its closure signals a significant blow to independent journalism in Russia.

items.title: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
items.summary: Six people died after a helicopter crashed in a northern Indian state, reportedly losing contact shortly after taking off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath. Authorities are investigating the incident.

items.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
items.summary: Spain's transport minister, Óscar Puente, has refused to resign despite calls for his departure after two high-speed trains collided, killing at least 69 people. The minister faces ongoing pressure following the week's rail disaster.

items.title: Student-backed election winners demand sweeping resignations in Serbia

items.summary: A Swedish academic, Andreas Malm, claims he has been barred from entering the UK to speak at an event alongside a Palestine Action co-founder. This raises concerns about freedom of speech and entry policies.

items.title: Syrians struggle with soaring prices as crisis challenges post-Assad recovery
items.summary: Syrians are facing soaring prices and the end of subsidies, driving discontent and challenging support for Ahmed al-Sharaa's government in its post-Assad recovery efforts. This situation highlights economic struggles and political instability in the region.

items.title: Three dead after two helicopters collide midair near Oregon airport
items.summary: Three people died in Oregon after two helicopters, a Robinson R22 and an Airbus, collided midair and crashed in a field adjacent to a highway. The accident occurred on Thursday afternoon.

items.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution

items.summary: US tech stocks experienced sharp declines, with Intel shares falling and the Nasdaq reaching a two-month low, as concerns grow over AI spending approaching $1 trillion. This market reaction reflects investor apprehension about the massive investments required for AI.

items.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Machado calls for elections upon return
items.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado, returning from nearly a year in exile, called for elections and declared that the transition in Venezuela's government would be "irreversible, organised, pacific." She seeks a democratic path forward for the country.

items.title: Watch: Why Australia's mushroom murderer may now die in prison
items.summary: Judges upheld the prosecution's appeal that Erin Patterson's initial non-parole period of 33 years was insufficient, meaning Australia's mushroom murderer may now die in prison. This decision follows her failed attempt to overturn her convictions.

items.summary: The introduction of AI is reportedly "deskilling" Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) rather than replacing them, suggesting a shift in required expertise or responsibilities. This trend indicates a transformation in technical roles due to AI adoption.

items.summary: Alaska's Senate race is embroiled in claims that Democrats recruited a "spoiler candidate" to confuse voters, prompting the governor to order an investigation. Separately, Hegseth has ousted an Army general as the US prepares for potential attacks on Iran.

items.summary: Blockchain intelligence firms have linked North Korea to the $6.3 billion hack on Binance, which was reported by the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. This investigation confirms the suspected state actor behind the major cyberattack.

items.summary: Democrats are working to weaken the Republican lead in state legislatures, recognizing that these bodies control most laws on critical issues like taxes, abortion, crime, and schools. This effort targets the significant impact of state-level politics.

items.title: For voters from immigrant families and new citizens, voting is bigger than themselves
items.summary: For voters from immigrant families and new citizens, the act of voting is often about more than economic concerns, extending to broader political calculations. Their participation highlights a profound commitment to civic engagement beyond personal financial stakes.

items.title: Here are the Senate races to watch ahead of Election Day

items.summary: Reports indicate a surge in ICE activity ahead of the midterms, raising concerns among advocates, but voter turnout is also surging across the country. This dual surge suggests a complex interaction between enforcement efforts and civic engagement.

items.summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro is aiming for a strong finish in his reelection campaign, which carries significant implications for a potential 2028 presidential bid, especially if he secures a Democratic trifecta in the state. His nationalized rhetoric and efforts to flip congressional seats indicate broader political ambitions.

items.title: Poll: Americans don’t trust polls
items.summary: A new POLITICO Poll reveals that only 25% of Americans trust political surveys to correctly estimate votes, reflecting widespread distrust fueled by past inaccuracies and challenges in reaching Republican voters. Despite this, a majority of voters still say they would vote even if polls showed their candidate far behind.

items.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy predicts Prime Video is on track to generate "tens of billions of dollars," attributing its success partly to blockbuster hits. This forecast indicates Amazon's high expectations for its streaming service's financial performance.

items.summary: Reddit is transitioning to a logged-in-only experience as AI changes how people find information online, aiming to protect its audience and business model. This strategic shift is in response to declining search traffic and evolving digital consumption habits.

items.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy believes AWS will become a $1 trillion business, but this growth requires significant capital expenditure as Amazon aims to dominate AI cloud computing. The company plans to spend big to achieve its goal of being the leader in AI infrastructure.

items.summary: Runware is developing a factory to mass-produce prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line, aiming for rapid deployment within 48 hours. The startup faces the challenge of proving its ability to deliver AI infrastructure at scale.

items.summary: DoorDash reported receiving only "several hundred" orders from third-party AI agents, indicating a cautious openness to collaborating with AI agent makers. This suggests the integration of AI agents into food delivery services is still in its early stages.

items.title: Elon Musk is ‘truly a genius,’ says Vladimir Putin
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin called Elon Musk "truly a genius" and confirmed "close contact" with him regarding Rassvet, Russia's Starlink-like satellite connectivity project. This statement highlights a unusual connection between the leaders of a nation and a prominent tech entrepreneur.

items.title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers’ private data
items.summary: General Motors reached a $220 million settlement regarding the sale of drivers' private data, mandating express consent from drivers before collecting or sharing their driving and location information. This settlement addresses concerns over data privacy practices in the automotive industry.

items.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach
items.summary: Hackers working for North Korea are suspected of being responsible for the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto breach, allegedly gaining access via a Binance employee's laptop. This incident marks one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in history.

items.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
items.summary: Rivian expanded its joint venture with Volkswagen to include an AI assistant, though details on whether this will increase the venture's $5.8 billion value were not disclosed. This signifies an increased focus on AI integration within their automotive collaboration.

items.summary: The cautionary Theranos tale takes on a new significance in the AI era, when companies that have never turned a profit are raising capital at trillion-dollar valuations.

items.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the UK
items.summary: Waymo plans to test self-driving Toyota bZ4X electric vehicles in Japan starting next year, expanding its partnership with the automaker to also include the UK. This collaboration further solidifies Waymo's global ambitions for robotaxi services.

items.title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
items.summary: A University of Kentucky administrator, David Durman, successfully obtained a religious exemption from using AI in his workplace. This case highlights the emerging legal and ethical considerations around AI implementation in professional settings.

items.title: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
items.summary: Zest's new AI concierge agent can find restaurants, combine group tastes, facilitate voting on options, and book reservations via text. This service aims to simplify the decision-making process for dining out.

items.title: Douglas Murray: Bibi Derangement Syndrome Is Spreading
items.summary: Douglas Murray asserts that "Bibi Derangement Syndrome" causes consistent underestimation of Benjamin Netanyahu's popularity, highlighting his enduring political survival despite opinion polls. Netanyahu's long tenure as prime minister contrasts with public perception and forecasts.

items.title: How Trump Can Fight Iran After the Midterms
items.summary: President Trump faces five options regarding Iran after the midterm elections, ranging from making a deal to continuing economic warfare, with military escalation posing a risk to financial markets and Republican candidates. The article examines the strategic choices available to the administration concerning Iran's Strait of Hormuz and nuclear program.

items.title: Is Nicki Minaj Trump’s Next Press Secretary?
items.summary: Rumors suggest rapper Nicki Minaj could be President Trump’s next press secretary after he publicly endorsed her at a Michigan rally, praising her appearance. This speculative news item explores the possibility of an unconventional appointment.

items.title: The Sane Person’s Guide to Microplastics
items.summary: Microplastics are pervasive in daily life, and a recent study in *Nature* suggests common plastics can generate harmful free radicals when in contact with water, potentially damaging cells and linking to diseases. While eliminating plastic is difficult, research continues into its health impacts.

items.title: Undo Legal Weed? Massachusetts Is Thinking About It.
items.summary: Massachusetts voters will decide on Question 8, which could make recreational cannabis illegal again, despite the state's marijuana industry generating $10 billion in revenue since 2018. Concerns about rising psychiatric emergency visits among young people and cannabis hyperemesis syndrome are driving the effort to reverse legalization.

items.title: Truth, Fact, and the Patterning of Reality: Virginia Woolf on How We Come to Know the World
items.summary: Virginia Woolf argues that truth is not merely an emergent property of facts but is perceived with all our faculties, not just intellect, and is multifarious yet unitary. She emphasizes that understanding the world involves our entire lived experience, beyond rational analysis.

items.title: When Your Parents Are Dying: Some of the Simplest, Most Difficult and Redemptive Life-Advice You’ll Ever Receive
items.summary: Mary Gaitskill advises spending time with dying parents, recognizing the profound emotional experience that transcends personality and reveals the fundamental mystery of human existence. This presence honors their essential connection to one's selfhood, even in difficult relationships.

items.title: Pope Leo calls for the disarmament of AI: ‘Machines are tools, not persons’
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV urged United Nations member states to "disarm" AI systems and take steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons, stressing that "Machines are tools, not persons." His address reinforces earlier calls to safeguard the human person in the age of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
items.summary: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe emphasized the company's autonomous vehicle ambitions, with a point-to-point hands-free driving feature rolling out to employees in 2026 and customers in 2027, followed by robotaxi launches with Uber in 2028. The next two years will be critical in determining Rivian's success in this high-stakes venture.

items.title: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru
items.summary: Starbucks is exploring using AI to provide personalized digital menus at drive-thrus, recognizing customers and offering tailored options. This initiative aligns with similar experiments by other fast-food chains like Taco Bell and McDonald's to enhance the drive-thru experience.

items.title: The delightfully messy state of Apple gadgets
items.summary: Apple is currently in a phase of significant gadget experimentation, introducing features like more iPhone screens, a MacBook touchscreen, and CarPlay apps for HomeView. While not always perfect, this period of innovation is seen as an exciting shift for the successful product maker.

items.title: Vizio’s discounted Mini LED TV lets you skip the sign-ups and smarts
items.summary: Vizio's Mini LED Quantum TV, available at Walmart, offers good brightness and vivid colors for its low price, with options to bypass smart TV features and privacy agreements during setup. However, it compromises on black levels due to its IPS panel and has only HDMI 2.0 ports.

items.title: Waymo’s next robotaxi is a purpose-built Toyota bZ4X
items.summary: Waymo announced a partnership with Toyota to use purpose-built bZ4X electric vehicles for a robotaxi service in Tokyo, with self-driving sensors and computers integrated directly on the assembly line.
